summary: Git archaeology in cm-main confirms two real problems. First, PR #1294's claim is correct: src/store-directory.ts:251 still uses the broken prefix check `escapeRel.startsWith('..')` for symlink-escape detection, introduced by #687 (2026-05-24). A later, correct fix exists in src/security.ts:710 (`rel === '..' || rel.startsWith('..' + sep)`), added by #852 (2026-06-22) for a different function, isPathInsideProject. The correct pattern was never carried over to store-directory.ts. ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2 verdict 'covered-by-test' for #1294 is wrong: the production bug is still live in v1 HEAD and the fix pattern already exists but is not applied where the bug is. Second, DECISIONS-r3 Q1 says v2 'keeps v1 #529 (855e330d)' for external MCP tool hints. 855e330d is the ORIGINAL one-shot nudge (2026-05-12). Four days later, #593 / 752d5236 (2026-05-16) replaced that one-shot nudge with a periodic one because the one-shot was silently dropped by context compaction in MCP-heavy sessions, letting large tool payloads flood context unchecked (reported: 55 Jira calls growing a session from 24K to 75K tokens). Q1 cites only the commit that caused that regression, not the fix. If v2 implements Q1 literally against 855e330d, it reintroduces the #593 bug. This is a blocker unless Q1 is amended to point at 752d5236 (periodic re-fire, default every 10 calls, env-tunable) instead.

items.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: f7499570 'feat(ctx_index): support directory paths with bounded traversal (#687)' (2026-05-24) added src/store-directory.ts:251 `if (escapeRel.startsWith('..') || resolve(escapeRel) === resolved) { if (escapeRel.startsWith('..')) continue; }`. ORIGINAL_INTENT (code comment at line 248): 'Symlink-escape: refuse to follow if the resolved target leaves rootReal.' The intent was correct, the implementation is a string-prefix check, which is exactly what PR #1294 reports breaking a symlink target literally named `..notes` (its relative path starts with the two characters `..` without ever climbing a directory). REGRESSION_RISK: a later, CORRECT version of this exact check exists in src/security.ts:710 (added by #852, 2026-06-22, for isPathInsideProject): `if (rel === '..' || rel.startsWith('..' + sep)) return false;` — using path.relative plus an explicit separator so a same-level name starting with `..` is not misflagged. That correct pattern was never backported to store-directory.ts. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: v2's directory-walk containment check must reuse isPathInsideProject's component-based logic, not reintroduce the #687 string-prefix bug.
regressions: store-directory.ts:251 still has the #687 bug as of v1 HEAD
related_closed_issues: #852 fixed the same class of bug in security.ts but did not touch store-directory.ts

items.recommendation: ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2's verdict of 'covered-by-test' for #1294 is wrong — the bug is unfixed in v1 HEAD. v2 must route directory-walk symlink checks through security.ts's isPathInsideProject rather than keep a second, broken implementation.

items.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY (related code, not this exact PR): hooks/ensure-deps.mjs has a long regression chain in v1 history: 6a7a6b2e (#172, shared dep bootstrap), bfbc4df1 (closes #206, auto-rebuild), cf2c7ea3 (#225, macOS codesign), 256f631f (#215, refactor), 442ccde7 (#238, ABI cache validation), f351fd1a (#331, skip on Node>=22.5/Bun), d328c247 (#318, tighten detection), 337ad7eb (#344, Windows ENOENT/EINVAL), 5432575a (#408/#410, Windows self-heal), 637d0bd4 (#446, stale ABI repair), 6471cf3b (#540, skip rebuild on modern Node), 33d0a470 (closes #543, Bun ABI seed), 28d58774 (#591, atomic binary swap). ORIGINAL_INTENT (6a7a6b2e): fix missing better-sqlite3 in plugin cache across hosts. REGRESSION_RISK: this file has been touched by a native-binary bug roughly every few weeks across two years; it encodes a large amount of host-specific knowledge (Windows ENOENT, Bun ABI, macOS codesign, Node>=22.5 skip). D2 says 'no runtime installs' in v2, which removes ensure-deps.mjs wholesale rather than fixing one more bug in it. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: if v2 ships better-sqlite3 (or any native module) at all, removing ensure-deps without an equivalent prebuilt-binary strategy risks reopening every one of the 13 issues above on the hosts that triggered them (Windows, Bun, macOS, old Node).
regressions: If v2 still ships a native dependency, dropping ensure-deps without a replacement reopens the entire #172...#591 chain
items.question: Does v2 ship better-sqlite3 or any other native module? If yes, what replaces ensure-deps' self-heal for Windows/Bun/macOS ABI mismatches?
items.recommendation: ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2's closed-by-design (ADR-0002, 'no runtime installs') is only safe if v2 either drops the native dependency entirely (e.g. pure-JS or WASM sqlite) or ships a prebuilt binary per platform at install time. If v2 still needs a native better-sqlite3 binary and relies on it 'just working', this is a blocker — re-verify against the actual v2 storage engine choice before closing #1281, #1253, #1278.

items.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 855e330d (#532, closes #529, 2026-05-12) added a one-shot guidanceOnce() nudge for Bash/Read/Grep AND external-MCP tools alike. ORIGINAL_INTENT: tell the agent once per session to route large tool output. REGRESSION_RISK found and resolved later by 752d5236 (#593, 2026-05-16): the commit message explicitly separates the two cases — 'Bash/Read/Grep nudges keep their one-shot behavior — they advise on tool *category* usage, not per-call flood pressure,' while only the external-MCP nudge was switched to periodic because repeated large external-tool payloads (55 Jira calls, 24K->75K tokens) kept flooding context after the single nudge was compacted away. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: the big-Read-hint-once-per-session design in ADR-0008 matches the authors' own post-#593 distinction (Read is a category hint, not a per-call flood risk), so this specific PR's target (#1270, Read hint cadence) is correctly closed-by-design and r2's verdict stands.
items.recommendation: r2's closed-by-design verdict for #1270 is correct and confirmed by archaeology. See #1231 below for the adjacent item that is NOT correctly settled.
